Beyond county averages: school-level disparities in Illinois

2014-15 through 2025-26 | Updated November 6, 2026 | Original state school data only

Aim 1: Coverage and disparities within counties

We mapped county-average coverage together with three measures of school-to-school disparity: median-P10 gap, enrollment-weighted SD and MAD. Each measure is shown before, during and after the pandemic. Coverage categories are <95%, 95-<97% and >=97%; disparity categories use pre-pandemic thirds, held fixed across periods.

Data: whole-school measles protection (PreK-12). Period values average annual measures. Grey indicates incomplete county data.

Aim 2: Changes across periods

We compared the same 102 counties across the pre-pandemic, pandemic and post-pandemic periods using four measures: median-P10 gap, enrollment-weighted SD, MAD and unweighted SD. Friedman tests compare all three periods; paired Wilcoxon tests compare periods two at a time. We report median paired changes with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. Pairwise p-values are Holm-adjusted within each measure.

Aim 3: Changes by baseline coverage and school size

We compared school coverage before, during and after the pandemic. Plots A and B use available schools in the 102-county comparison set. Plots C and D follow the same 4,312 schools and compare each school with its pre-pandemic average.

For C and D, groups are fixed from baseline. Positive decline means lower coverage; negative decline means improvement. Changes are in percentage points.

Is the median change different from zero?

We resampled whole counties 4,000 times, keeping their schools together. An interval entirely above zero supports a decline; entirely below zero supports improvement; crossing zero means the direction is unclear. These are individual 95% intervals, without adjustment for multiple comparisons.

Methods, data checks and limitations
  1. Population: Illinois school measles protection, all grades PreK-12. This is the available proxy for the requested MMR outcome; it is not a combined MMR or kindergarten-only measure.
  2. Years: 2014-15 through 2025-26. Main comparison: the same 102 of 102 counties in all 12 years; Chicago is combined with suburban Cook. All 102 counties are represented in every year.
  3. Periods: Pre 2014-15 to 2019-20; Pandemic 2020-21 to 2022-23; Post 2023-24 to 2025-26. Labels describe timing, not proof of pandemic causation or recovery.
  4. County annual metrics: unweighted median minus R type-7 10th percentile; enrollment-weighted population SD; raw/unscaled MAD (constant=1); unweighted sample SD as an additional comparison. One-school gap/MAD/weighted SD are zero; sample SD is undefined. Secondary sample-SD period means omit unavailable annual SDs (Jasper has one school in 2016-17 and 2020-21); the three specified disparity metrics remain defined.
  5. County average = enrollment-weighted school coverage. Student burden = enrollment share in schools <95%, 95-<97%, or >=97%. The upper category includes exactly 97%, resolving the ambiguous threshold wording consistently with Aim 3. Enrollment means all school students, not only unvaccinated students.
  6. Period county values average annual metrics with equal weight per school year. They do not pool all school-years into one distribution. County summaries give each county equal weight; county median burdens do not add to 100%.
  7. Aim 1 map categories: county-average coverage uses <95%, 95-<97%, and >=97%. Each disparity measure uses its own pre-pandemic county tertiles (type-7 33rd and 67th percentiles), held fixed across all three periods. These are relative descriptive categories, not clinical risk thresholds. Exact cutoffs are saved in main/aim1_map_cutoffs.csv; legend labels are rounded to three decimals.
  8. Tests: Friedman repeated-county comparisons across three periods; paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with normal approximation and continuity correction. Pairwise p-values receive Holm correction over three comparisons per metric; omnibus p-values are also Holm-adjusted across eight metrics. Signed-rank tests concern paired-difference distributions, not solely their medians.
  9. Effect size: median of within-county paired differences, with percentile bootstrap 95% CIs from 4,000 resamples of whole counties (seed 20261105). These are descriptive resampling intervals for the observed county set; they do not incorporate data errors or spatial dependence.
  10. Plot C/D confidence intervals: 4,000 county-cluster bootstrap resamples (seed 20261106). Sample all 102 matched-cohort counties with replacement and keep each sampled county's schools, fixed baseline coverage/size groups and both follow-up changes together. Calculate the school-level median decline within each group for each replicate; report percentile 95% CIs. The eight intervals per plot are individual, not adjusted for multiple comparisons. Counties are treated as independent; resampling does not correct baseline selection or regression to the mean.
  11. Sensitivity restrictions: include a county only if it has >=5 or >=10 valid-coverage school records in every one of the 12 years. Every main plot and county comparison is repeated under both restrictions.
  12. School distributions (3A/B): calculate annual 0.5-percentage-point histograms and average annual shares within each period. This avoids giving the longer Pre period extra weight. School shares count all usable coverage records; student shares exclude missing/suppressed enrollment.
  13. School changes (3C/D): 4312 schools with stable assigned county, >=3 usable pre-period years, and all three years in each follow-up period. Baseline coverage/enrollment are available-year pre-period averages. Fixed coverage groups: <90%, 90-<95%, 95-<97%, >=97%; fixed size groups: <250, 250-499, 500-999, >=1,000. Decline = baseline minus follow-up mean, in percentage points; positive means worse coverage. Enrollment-weighted mean changes use fixed baseline enrollment. The panel follows schools, not the same individual students.
  14. Variance decomposition: use the same matched schools and school period-average coverage. Within each county, total population variance = within-baseline-group variance + between-group variance. Baseline-group contributions are sums of squared distances to the county mean divided by county school count; they add exactly to the total. Equal-county mean contribution changes are reported. This differs from annual weighted-SD estimands.
  15. 2014-15: 4873 original ISBE school records, with original RCDTS IDs. County is assigned from the state ID county code, consistently with all later years. No authors' school records or inferred IDs are used.
  16. Coverage comparability: 2020-21 uses protected / total enrollment rather than source percentages that excluded remote noncompliant students. The same protected / total enrollment definition is used in 2014-15: all 4,843 checkable school rows reproduce the reported percentage when the denominator sums only numeric status counts, ignoring suppressed <10 entries; 3,940 reported values differ from protected / enrollment by >0.01 pp. Rows with suppressed counts preventing consistent calculation are excluded. Reported 2014-15 percentages are retained in a sensitivity check. Other years use reported coverage. The main analysis retains previously reconstructed enrollment for 458 Chicago records in 2021-22; these are estimates. Extra checks exclude estimated-enrollment rows, known conflicting records, and 2014-15, and compare reported 2020-21 values.
  17. Limitations: source changes, suppression, partial pre-period school records, possible ID reuse/mergers, cohort selection, regression to the mean, and spatially correlated counties. There is no causal estimate of COVID effects. Findings do not measure outbreaks or transmission.
  18. Reproducibility: raw and existing processed datasets remain unchanged. Source-file MD5 checksums are checked before and after the analysis. New analysis-ready extracts, linkage audits, exclusions, tests, confidence intervals, plots (PNG/PDF), and session information are saved separately.

Statistical documentation: Friedman test; paired Wilcoxon test; Holm adjustment.

Reproduce with scripts/il_run_state_only.R. All numerical results, sample flow and linkage audits are in this report directory. Individual figures are available as PNG and PDF.
